title: K-injective resolutions compute derived functors
statement: Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive] functor between Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] and let $K\in\operatorname{Ch}^+(\mathcal A)$. Then: (1) Any two K-injective resolutions [def-sp-kinjective-bridge] of $K$ are homotopy equivalent under $K$, uniquely up to homotopy; hence $v(I)\cong v(J)$ canonically in the homotopy category, $RvK$ is well defined up to canonical isomorphism, and it is functorial in $K$. (2) A bounded-below complex of injective objects is K-injective. Thus an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $X\to I^\bullet$ is a K-injective resolution of $X[0]$ and $\mathcal H^p(Rv(X[0]))\cong R^pv(X)$ for every $p$. (3) $Rv(K[n])\cong(RvK)[n]$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism $s:A\to B$ and a K-injective complex $I$, precomposition $s^*:\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(B,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(A,I)$ is bijective by [lem-sp-kinjective-comparison-principle].

Apply the comparison principle to the two resolution maps. Surjectivity gives comparison maps under K; injectivity gives uniqueness and shows their composites equal identities in the homotopy category. Lift these equalities to homotopies. Applying the additive functor to the homotopies gives the displayed inverse morphisms and isomorphism after quotienting. For each morphism of bounded-below complexes choose its comparison lift. Uniqueness proves the identity law; compose the equations under the resolution maps to prove the composition law. This defines the functor on the prescribed chosen resolutions, with identity objectwise comparison isomorphisms.

Grothendieck abelian categories have enough injectives, hence chosen ordinary injective resolutions exist. Mathlib CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective proves K-injectivity of each bounded-below complex of injectives. The extension to integer degrees of an InjectiveResolution augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism and its target is K-injective, by the existing Mathlib instances. Compare any chosen K-injective resolution of X[0] with this extension using the comparison principle. Apply HomotopyCategory.homologyFunctor to the resulting mapped comparison isomorphism and use homologyFunctorFactors at both endpoints. HomologicalComplex.mapExtendIso (WeilConjectures.FromJoel.Algebra.Homology.Embedding.ExtendMap) identifies F of the extended injective resolution with the extension of F of the resolution. HomologicalComplex.extendHomologyIso identifies its integer-degree p homology with its natural-degree p homology. InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj identifies the latter with (F.rightDerived p).obj X.

The shift of a K-injective complex is K-injective and the shift of a quasi-isomorphism is a quasi-isomorphism. Use the shift compatibility isomorphism of CochainComplex.Plus.ι to regard the shifted augmentation as a resolution of (K[n]).obj. Compare the given resolution of K[n] with this shifted resolution. Apply F termwise and the homotopy quotient to get the comparison isomorphism, then compose with the commShiftIso of F.mapHomologicalComplex and of HomotopyCategory.quotient.

proof_origin.place: Proof clauses (1)--(3), realized in Lean by N1 using Mathlib homotopy quotient, shift, and homology APIs and the existing mapExtendIso

blueprint_notes.label: status
blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** The source proved the agreement in (2) by saying that a
Cartan--Eilenberg resolution refines both routes, which made this lemma and
the Cartan--Eilenberg theorem [thm-sp-if-e1] depend on each other. Nothing
below uses a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution: (1) and (3) are formal
consequences of K-injectivity, and (2) needs only that an injective
resolution of an object is a bounded-below complex of injectives. The
theorem now cites this lemma and not the other way round.

split_report.summary: Replaced the imported proof sketch with four explicit steps. The comparison principle is a new Mathlib leaf; bounded-below injectivity and shifts cite existing Mathlib leaves, and object-level agreement follows the stated definitions.
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the opening comparison principle and clauses (1), (2), and (3) of the blueprint proof.

tool_uses.why: Its Mathlib leaf supplies bounded-below injective-complex K-injectivity used in clause (2).
